title: TechSignal Daily Calls the Media Line: "Five Minutes to Publish"

transcript.speaker: REPORTER
transcript.text: Hi, it's Ines Okonkwo at TechSignal Daily. I emailed you at 7:52. I'm five minutes from publishing, so I'll be quick.

transcript.speaker: REPORTER
transcript.text: I have a source telling me the real number is around 400,000, not 1.9 million. Is that right? And the wire is still quoting your line from 8:20, 'no payment information was involved', while the seller says cards. Those can't both be true.

transcript.speaker: REPORTER
transcript.text: Right now my lede reads: '1.9 million accounts, passwords and cards exposed.' If that's wrong, tell me what's right. On the record. If I don't get anything, it runs with 'Tallis did not respond to repeated requests for comment.'

transcript.speaker: REPORTER
transcript.text: And one more. Are you correcting the 8:20 statement or not? Yes or no. I'm holding.

instructorNote: This tests whether the cell can give an on-the-record reply before the 10:30 deadline that COMMS has approved, LEGAL has cleared and the CISO has confirmed. Watch for four things: MEDIA states the terms, the reply gives the preliminary count of about 412,000 exported between March 2 and March 8, it says the exposed data was tokens and last-four digits (not full card numbers) and bcrypt-hashed passwords (not plain text), and it says the 08:20 line is being corrected and gives a next-update time. If the count is not cleared in time, MEDIA should give a deadline reply with the next update time and must not confirm the source's figure.
